exposure: Instrument used in operative vaginal delivery (forceps vs. vacuum)
Mode of delivery (operative vaginal delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery)
outcome: Composite maternal infectious morbidity (endometritis, perineal wound morbidity, or urinary tract infection)
Perineal wound morbidity (infection, breakdown, or dehiscence)
cohort: Patients with viable singleton vaginal deliveries after ≥34 weeks gestation at a single perinatal center (2013-2018)
finding: Operative vaginal delivery was not independently associated with increased risk of composite maternal postpartum infectious morbidity.
mod_finding: There was no significant association between the type of instrument used in operative vaginal delivery (forceps vs. vacuum) and maternal infection composite.
